facts.facts: VeriRail is a financial freeze and dispute protection prototype for consumers and businesses. Recovery likelihood uses consumer complaint history, the incident description and evidence signals. Payment risk uses transaction features. Tools compare historical provider outcomes and produce dispute-letter drafts, case briefs, case snapshots, audit results and model explanations. The app cannot access real accounts, freeze or release funds, submit payments, send letters, or guarantee outcomes.

facts.topics: model neural architecture training dataset accuracy fairness bias audit
facts.facts: The supplied notebook trains Gate 2 on Bob-68/cfpb-consumer-complaints from Hugging Face and Gate 1 on IEEE-CIS fraud-detection transaction data from Kaggle. Gate 2 embeds a masked description with bge-small-en-v1.5, then combines text and provider/evidence features using FiLM. Gate 1 uses exported neural weights on payment features. Audit evaluates benchmarks and false positives. Protected demographics and the remote/digital proxy are not used as VeriRail payment inference inputs; omission does not prove universal fairness. Spectral-GRL and dCor are debiasing techniques in the project.

facts.topics: score odds uncertainty estimate recovery baseline relief surge conformal
facts.facts: Recovery odds estimate likelihood of relief, not a dollar refund. Provider baseline is historical adjusted relief for the selected product. Harm Surge compares recent and longer-period complaint activity. The uncertainty note can be likely, unlikely, or uncertain; historical conformal coverage is not an individual guarantee. Provider and evidence comparison effects are separate and are not additive.

facts.topics: payment triage transaction risk step-up clear block csv split
facts.facts: Payment Triage scores a scenario from amount, channel, history, and surge. Clear, Step-Up, and Block are simulated decisions, not live provider instructions. Step-Up suggests more verification. CSV Batch accepts payment rows with id,amount,channel,past_txns,past_avg,remote. It is not a document uploader. Split Check is a simulation, not permission to evade provider checks.

facts.topics: case evidence receipt document narrative dispute letter steps action plan deadline
facts.facts: Next steps are: check the incident description and actual evidence; prepare and review a letter draft; send it yourself through the provider’s official dispute channel; save a snapshot and keep references and responses. There is no three-year plan. The 1,2,3 numbers are workflow steps. Only apply suggested evidence clauses if true. There is no receipt upload or document verification. The original framework and escalation suggestions are under Timing & escalation; actual deadlines depend on the incident and rules and must be confirmed.

facts.topics: privacy security data saved workspace login sign-in authentication
facts.facts: Recognized dates, card numbers, SSNs, and email patterns are masked in-browser before embedding, but pattern matching can miss personal data. Account and snapshot storage uses browser localStorage and is not production-grade server authentication or encrypted multi-device storage. Google sign-in needs an OAuth client ID. Financial scoring runs in-browser. Open-ended Project AI sends the question, recent chat, and relevant masked workspace context through the app server to its configured AI provider. The provider key stays on the server. The user should remove unnecessary personal details.

facts.topics: safe rails bank provider compare diversification business
facts.facts: Safe Rails compares provider history for the selected product using adjusted relief and surge measures and includes a diversification simulation. These are retrospective/model comparisons, not a ranking of current rates, fees, all banks, or guarantees that a provider is safe.

facts.topics: features design interface themes mobile cursor qr accessibility
facts.facts: The six tools are Dispute Recovery, Payment Triage, Safe Rails, Neural Lab, Audit, and QR & System. Sidebar navigation, a mobile menu, light and black dark themes, Inspect, and a non-clicking AI pointer help users. QR codes share a hosted app URL. Snapshot, Copy Brief, Draft letter, Bias Check, CSV download, and QR download retain their original controls. The pointer only navigates, highlights, and focuses a known control; it does not fill, click, send, or pay for the user.

controls.title: Change the appearance
controls.action: Use the theme button in the top header to switch light or dark mode.

controls.title: Manage your workspace
controls.action: Open the workspace button in the top header. Choose Switch Account / Sign Out to return to the sign-in screen.

controls.title: Review the privacy preview
controls.action: Review the masked model input below the description. Remove unnecessary personal details from your description yourself. Saved snapshots stay in this browser workspace.

controls.title: Copy the case brief
controls.action: Choose “Copy Brief” and paste it into your own document. Review it before sharing.

controls.title: Run a bias check
controls.action: Choose “Bias Check” beside the case actions, then read the comparison that appears below.

controls.title: Start with your provider
controls.action: Choose the provider and product involved, then describe what happened.

controls.title: Choose a provider and product
controls.action: Select the company involved and the product below it.

controls.title: Describe what happened
controls.action: Replace the sample with your account of the incident. Include the date, amount, case reference, and documents you actually have.

controls.title: Set the time since the incident
controls.action: Move the slider to the number of days since the incident. Check the relevant rules for your product; the prototype’s timing prompts are not a confirmed deadline.

controls.title: Understand your recovery estimate
controls.action: Read the percentage and uncertainty note, then check Missing Evidence for useful next steps.

controls.title: Read the uncertainty note
controls.action: Review the note alongside the percentage. Add accurate supporting evidence if it is available.

controls.title: Review missing evidence
controls.action: Check the suggestions. Use “+ Apply” only if the suggested statement is true and supported by your records, then review the text.

controls.title: Follow your next steps
controls.action: Start with “Check your case”, then open a letter draft. Save the result when the model is ready. You review and send the letter through the provider’s official dispute channel.

controls.title: Draft a dispute letter
controls.action: Choose “Draft letter”, review the wording and details, then copy or download it. VeriRail does not send the letter for you.

controls.title: Save a case snapshot
controls.action: Choose “Save snapshot”. Find it in Saved Snapshots below. Review it before sharing a device.

controls.title: Find your saved snapshots
controls.action: Scroll through Saved Snapshots. Workspace controls in the header let you switch accounts or clear saved snapshots.

controls.title: Check a payment
controls.action: Enter the amount and channel, then set the real transaction history. Read the simulated decision to the right.

controls.title: Read the payment decision
controls.action: Read Clear, Step-Up, or Block alongside the risk score. A simulated Clear does not guarantee that a provider will release a payment.

controls.title: Explore the split simulation
controls.action: Review the modeled comparison. It does not authorize bypassing provider checks or guarantee clearance.

controls.title: Understand the decision thresholds
controls.action: Compare the marker with the labeled regions and inspect the contributing factors below.

controls.title: Check multiple payments with CSV
controls.action: Paste or upload a CSV using the sample column names. Choose “Score CSV”, review the results, and download them if needed.

controls.title: Compare payment providers
controls.action: Choose Provider A, Provider B, and a product. Review both result cards and their limitations.

controls.title: Inspect provider context
controls.action: Review the scale and shift visualization for the active provider.

controls.title: Explore phrase contributions
controls.action: Review the highlighted phrases. Interpret them as model behavior, not proof that a claim is valid.

controls.title: Compare the same case across providers
controls.action: Review the provider matrix using the same case description.

controls.title: Review model evaluation
controls.action: Compare the metrics and failure cases. Historical test performance does not guarantee future outcomes.

controls.title: Compare recovery benchmarks
controls.action: Read the benchmark table alongside the accuracy note and failure cases.

controls.title: Review false-positive freezes
controls.action: Compare the plotted rates and review the audit context.

controls.title: Review fairness and coverage
controls.action: Read disparity and coverage together. Removing protected inputs does not establish that every outcome is fair.

controls.title: Share the app with a QR code
controls.action: Enter the hosted URL, check the generated code, and choose “Download QR”. A localhost address will not open from someone else’s phone.

evaluation.warning: Historical test measurements are not a guarantee of individual or future outcomes.
